{{Short description|Analysis theorem}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Calderón–Zygmund lemma''' is a fundamental result in [[Fourier analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]], and [[singular integral]]s. It is named for the mathematicians [[Alberto Calderón]] and [[Antoni Zygmund]].

Given an [[integrable function]] {{math|''f'' : '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> → '''C'''}}, where {{math|'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>}} denotes [[Euclidean space]] and {{math|'''C'''}} denotes the [[complex numbers]], the [[lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] gives a precise way of [[partition of a set|partitioning]] {{math|'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>}} into two [[set (mathematics)|set]]s: one where {{math|''f''}} is essentially small; the other a [[countable set|countable]] collection of cubes where {{math|''f''}} is essentially large, but where some control of the function is retained.

This leads to the associated '''Calderón–Zygmund decomposition''' of {{math|''f''}}, wherein {{math|''f''}} is written as the sum of "good" and "bad" functions, using the above sets.

==Covering lemma==
<blockquote>Let {{math|''f'' : '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> → '''C'''}} be integrable and {{mvar|α}} be a positive constant. Then there exists an open set {{math|Ω}} such that:

:(1) {{math|Ω}} is a disjoint union of open cubes, {{math|Ω {{=}} ∪<sub>''k''</sub> ''Q<sub>k</sub>''}}, such that for each {{math|''Q<sub>k</sub>''}},

::<math>\alpha\le  \frac{1}{m(Q_k)} \int_{Q_k} |f(x)| \, dx \leq 2^d \alpha.</math>

:(2) {{math|{{!}}''f''(''x''){{!}} ≤ ''α''}} almost everywhere in the complement {{mvar|F}} of {{math|Ω}}.

Here, <math>m(Q_k)</math> denotes the [[Measure_(mathematics)|measure]] of the set <math>Q_k</math>.
</blockquote>

==Calderón–Zygmund decomposition==
<blockquote>Given {{math|''f''}} as above, we may write {{math|''f''}} as the sum of a "good" function {{mvar|g}} and a "bad" function {{mvar|b}}, {{math|''f'' {{=}} ''g'' + ''b''}}. To do this, we define

:<math>g(x) =  \begin{cases}f(x), & x \in F, \\ \frac{1}{m(Q_j)}\int_{Q_j}f(t)\,dt, & x \in Q_j,\end{cases}</math>

and let {{math|''b'' {{=}} ''f'' − ''g''}}. Consequently we have that

:<math>b(x) = 0,\ x\in F</math>
:<math>\frac{1}{m(Q_j)}\int_{Q_j} b(x)\, dx = 0</math>
 
for each cube {{math|''Q<sub>j</sub>''}}.</blockquote>

The function {{mvar|b}} is thus supported on a collection of cubes where {{math|''f''}} is allowed to be "large", but has the beneficial property that its average value is zero on each of these cubes. Meanwhile, {{math|{{!}}''g''(''x''){{!}} ≤ ''α''}} for almost every {{mvar|x}} in {{mvar|F}}, and on each cube in {{math|Ω}}, {{mvar|g}} is equal to the average value of {{math|''f''}} over that cube, which by the covering chosen is not more than {{math|2<sup>''d''</sup>''α''}}.
